texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2690368/ 1 Date of filing of Dar : 20.07.2018 Date of Decision : 25.04.2023 Award 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. As per the investigation by the police officials on 18.02.2018, complainant Jiledar Khan / claimant/ injured/ victim filed an complaint stating that on 07.12.2017 at about 06.00 AM, he was going on foot from his house at Gali no.25, Tughalakabad Extension, New Delhi to gali no. 24, Main Road, Ravidass Marg. At that time, one Omni Van bearing no.DL 3CZ 8663 from Majidia Hospital side in a rash and negligent manner and a high speed and hit such claimant. As as result he failed down on the road and become unconscious. The passerby took him in the same van and got admitted in Majidia Hospital. When his condition was getting worse, he was taken to Safdarjung Hospital. He was discharged from Safdarjung Hospital from 13.12.2017 and at that time, driver of such Omni car came to meet him and told his name as Sanjay. He further assured the injured that he will reimburse the medical treatment expenses. Further he gave mobile number 9310270540. Further there are two other phone number of Sanjay/ driver of offending vehicle MACT No.: 684/18 Jiledar Khan VS. Sanjay Gupta & Ors. Page No. 2 of 21 rpt :3: but as Sanjay did not reimbursed his medical expenses, the claimant filed the present complaint. 3. Accordingly, initially, police registered a case u/s 279, 337 IPC. 4. The police after investigation in present case filed charge sheet for offence u/s 279, 338, 201, 468 and 471 IPC against the respondent no.1. Present DAR was also filed by the investigating officer. 5. In this case, there was no third party insurance of such offending vehicle. 6. Further as per record, R-1 appeared and filed a reply. In nutshell, in reply, he denied that he was driver / owner of such offending vehicle / Omni Van. He further denied that he has any liability in the present case. He further stated that IO along with others wrongly implicated him in the present case. 7. Further as per record, after repeated attempts made only, registered owner of the vehicle Sh. Gul Mohd was produced by the IO but still he did not file any reply. Jiledar Khan vs . Sanjay Gupta & Ors. on 25 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2690368/ 2 8. From the material on record, the following issues were framed on 07.10.2021 by my Ld. Predecessor: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 07.02.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no.DL-3CZ 8663 being driven by R-1 & and owned by R-2? OPP 2. MACT No.: 684/18 Jiledar Khan VS. Sanjay Gupta & Ors. Page No. 3 of 21 rpt 9. Further, from record, it is revealed that in view of the MACT Rules and judgment by Hon'ble High Court and Hon'ble Supreme Court in this regard, a show-cause notice was given to respondent side to deposit security to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/- in this Tribunal. But they failed to offer any reasonable explanation to deposit the same. As such, their right to contest was closed. 10. Claimant/ injured filed his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents Ex. PW-1/1 to PW-1/8 (colly) including OPD cards, DAR, medical bills, MLC of concerned hospital and copy of Aadhar card, ITR returns. As per record, despite opportunity such witness was not cross-examined by respondent side. 11. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 15. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.

Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. Page No. 4 of 21 rpt further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. In National Insurance Co. Jiledar Khan vs . Sanjay Gupta & Ors. on 25 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2690368/ 3 Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 16. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. 21.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that MACT No.: 684/18 Jiledar Khan VS. In Abati Bezbaruah Vs. Geological Survey of India, (2003) 3 SCC 148, the following was held while interpreting section 171 of the MV Act, 1988:- Three decisions were cited before us by Mr. A. P. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his contentions. Neither Sec. 34 CPC nor Sec. 4-A(3) of Workmen's Compensation Act MACT No.: 684/18 Jiledar Khan VS. Sanjay Gupta & Ors. 26. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. 27. The total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs. Rs. 1,84,175/-/- with simple interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till its actual realization. 33. The expression used in guideline No. (iv) issued by this Court is that in the case of literate persons also the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i), whereas in the guideline Nos. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure MACT No.: 684/18 Jiledar Khan VS. Sanjay Gupta & Ors. Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit without recording that MACT No.: 684/18 Jiledar Khan VS.
